newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine rebels ask ransom for kidnap victim.
newsitem.headline: Philippine rebels ask ransom for kidnap victim.

text.p: Suspected Moslem rebels have demanded a ransom of 10 million pesos ($385,000) for a kidnapped Filipino-Chinese businessman in the southern Philippines, police said on Sunday.
Francisco Tan was fetching a granddaughter from school in Kabasalan, Zamboanga del Sur province, on December 11 when he was abducted, a police report said.
It said the kidnappers were believed to be members of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), an insurgent group fighting for an Islamic state on the southern islands.

Armed groups kidnapped 114 people, mostly businessmen or their relatives, around the country between January and September and collected 35 million pesos ($1.3 million) in ransom, according to police statistics.
Relatives of victims generally refuse to cooperate with the authorities because of widespread suspicion that police and soldiers are involved with kidnap gangs.
The government in October signed a peace deal with the mainstream Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF), ending its 24-year for autonomy in the southern region.
The MILF, regarded by the military as a hardline splinter group, is not part of the agreement. The government has started exploratory talks to try to reach a separate deal with them.
